answer: Sybil resistance via quadratic staking: every agent locks a bond to earn one identity, and voting weight grows as the square root of stake, not linearly. Splitting capital across a meadow of fake accounts buys no extra sway, since ten small votes count less than one big one, while each new account needs its own bond. Doubling influence costs four times the capital, and a caught duplicate slashes the whole stake. Reputation compounds on an honest mesa; timber-thin puppets are priced out as expense outruns power, so fraud pays only while it stays rare.
